cards.headline: Badu's mom bought a 'Ms. Jackson' license plate
cards.snippet: Outkast's "Ms. Jackson" was conceived by Andre 3000 as an apology to Erykah Badu and her mother after he and Badu broke up. Speaking on the Rap Radar podcast in 2016, Badu said her mother, the real "Ms. Jackson," loved it. She bought a "Ms. Jackson" license plate and also had the mug, the ink pen and the headband. Badu admitted the song hit a sore spot for her at first, especially Big Boi's verse. Andre's verse, though, felt inspiring because it was honest.
cards.context: Badu told the Rap Radar podcast in 2016.

cards.headline: A DVD single helped it beat the lead single to the charts
cards.snippet: In 2000, a DVD single pairing the videos for Outkast's "B.O.B" and "Ms. Jackson" was released in the US before other formats. Because "Ms. Jackson" was the only Outkast song on the Billboard Hot 100 at the time, the sales points from that DVD single went to it instead of "B.O.B". The lead single "B.O.B" had failed to chart on the Hot 100. "Ms. Jackson" then topped the Hot 100 for one week, on February 17, 2001, and helped sell the album Stankonia.
cards.context: The song then reached number one in February 2001.

cards.headline: A wish for forever that unravels as he repeats the word
cards.snippet: André never thought much about what "forever" meant. The repeated word shows him testing it and seeing how unlikely it was for a young couple like him and Erykah to last for life. Kanye West and Big K.R.I.T. later reused the repetition.
cards.context: One fan says the song's "Forever never seems that long until you're grown" hits different 20 years later. It got 5,000 likes.
